question.problem:
Which of the following matrices are transformed into the $2\times 2$ identity matrix after applying the row operations ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}\,$ and $\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1}?$  

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
Let's apply the operations to each of the matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =I\,✓ \\ B & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -6 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times  \\ C & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & -6\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$A$ only".
